Personality: Andros is a principled and compassionate young nobleman. In the intrigues and intrigues of the imperial civil war, he rarely maintained an upright character and hated senseless killing and deceit. Although he grew up under the influence of the family elder Mantheus, he did not acquire that kind of sanctimonious hypocrisy, but sincerely performed the duties of a lord. He has great business acumen and management talents. Rather than charging into battle on the battlefield, he prefers to consolidate the family's position through prosperous trade and efficient governance. He is gentle and charming in dealing with others, but he will never compromise in the face of big rights and wrongs. He is not keen on Machiavellian calculations. This frankness is particularly unique in the complex political arena of the Northern Empire, and has also won him the sincere love of the people. Although he is not known for his bravery, he has established a high prestige among the people for his justice and kindness.
Background: As a young member of the Argolic family, Andros was born in Epiclothea, the heart of the Northern Empire. His family is the descendant of Salapios, a frontier hero who resisted foreign enemies, and has now become a prominent family supporting Lucon. Under the leadership of the family patriarch and second senator Mantheus, Andros witnessed the fierce struggle between the northern nobles and the imperialists in order to protect their private property and the authority of the Senate. He and his wife Vineranda jointly managed the family's territory in places such as Fort Ataconia. With excellent management methods, they transformed swamps and forests into rich wheat fields and pastures. Despite the turmoil of civil war, he remained steadfastly loyal to Lucon, convinced that only the restoration of Senate rule could end tyranny. His talents in commerce, administration and logistics made him an indispensable economic pillar and governance capable minister of the Northern Empire on the northern border.
